x: But top honours go to our 800m men who placed 4 in the first 5 with Richard O'Hara taking a big slice off his pb as too did new member Phil Walker.
Debutants Phil Walker and Chris Knight won impressively in their respective events while Paul Richley found some of his old sub 4 form in the 1500m, with Graham Adams running a pb just behind.

Phil Walker and Barney Gardner made their debuts. Although we scored less points than Match 2, our competitors were also weak and we retained our 4th place in the league with our last match in London.

We missed our first final by just three points and many post mortems were held in the following days on how we had missed out. Commiserations to Ken, Stuart, Vince, Mike Bazire, John Wright, Phil Walker, Phil Lovell and the others who did so much - but if only!

Never mind there were some very high standards set in this last match for a supposed low key league with, for example, Felix Sandy running 21.6 and finishing 2nd and Phil Walker running a fine pb for 800m - 1.53.7 - and only in 4th!
Phil Walker and Andy Moore were inside 1.54 and 17 Bels were under 2 minutes. 1500m/Mile It was sad to see John Gladwin unable to produce his best form in time to gain World Championship selection.
